MB7389 · MILLIMETRES

Fix the sensor in position first. Measure from the same bucket-bottom datum. Preview measured settings first, then use Save calibration to Arduino to apply and persist them.

Measure the sensor face to the inside bottom with a ruler, enter the water limits below, then start monitoring and save to Arduino. Keep more than 300 mm clearance above the highest planned water level.

BROWSER PREVIEW · NOT FIRMWARE PERMISSION

Waiting for fresh samples

—

Save and confirm the Arduino settings.

Save calibration to Arduino writes the four measurements to EEPROM and restarts its water-level decisions. Settings survive power loss. The Arduino confirms the active values below. Older firmware requires the one-time upload; downloading config.h remains an alternative.

One firmware update is required to enable USB calibration.

Upload commands
"$task_cli" compile --fqbn arduino:avr:uno arduino/FarmbotWaterMonitor
"$task_cli" upload --fqbn arduino:avr:uno --port /dev/cu.usbserial-1310 arduino/FarmbotWaterMonitor

Disconnect the dashboard before uploading. Your USB port may change. Reconnect afterward and check that the firmware configuration matches.

These show the settings currently uploaded to the Uno. Use Save calibration to Arduino above and wait for confirmation to apply the browser measurements to the firmware. EEPROM settings take priority over config.h after restart.

Bucket test: what to measure

Fix the sensor above the water. Measure sensor face to bottom, maximum water depth, low-water trip and recovery depths. Keep a clear air gap in the sensor’s usable range. Distance decreases as water rises. A 300 mm reading can be minimum-range saturation.
